title: Bombay-ish Beans
style: Creamy, aromatic Indian-inspired beans with jammy onions and warm spices
description: Comforting, deeply flavoured beans cooked with whole spices, tomatoes, and a creamy nutty finish — rich without heaviness.

items.item: ground roasted peanuts or cashew butter

steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, and dried chilli. Let them crackle and become fragrant.
Add onion with a pinch of salt and cook 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until deeply soft, jammy, and lightly golden.
Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Stir in turmeric, ground cumin, coriander, and garam masala; toast briefly.
Add diced tomatoes and simmer about 5 minutes until thick and cooked down.
Add beans, vegetable stock, and ground peanuts or cashew butter. Simmer 10–12 minutes until creamy and cohesive.
Season well with salt. Stir in crushed kasuri methi, lemon juice, and most of the fresh coriander.
Finish with a swirl of coconut milk or vegan yoghurt if using, and scatter remaining coriander over the top.
tips: Long-cooked onions are non-negotiable — they’re the backbone of flavour.
Kasuri methi adds restaurant-level depth; a little goes a long way.
This thickens as it sits — loosen with hot water or stock if needed.
